items.followUp: Two bodies of masses 2 kg and 3 kg move together at 4 m/s. Find their total momentum.

rubric.why: Assesses the statement and condition of the law.
rubric.description: States that the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant when no external force acts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that total momentum remains constant and 1 mark for stating the no-external-force or isolated-system condition.

rubric.why: Assesses the interaction forces used to explain conservation.
rubric.description: States that the forces the two bodies exert on each other are equal and opposite.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct equal-and-opposite force statement or equation.

rubric.why: Assesses how the interaction leads to conservation of total momentum.
rubric.description: Explains that equal and opposite changes in momentum leave total momentum unchanged, so momentum before equals momentum after.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking equal and opposite momentum changes to equal total momentum before and after the interaction.

modelAnswer: For an isolated system, if no external force acts on it, its total momentum remains constant.
During an interaction between two bodies, the forces they exert on each other are equal and opposite: F1 = -F2.
Since force is the rate of change of momentum, the changes in the bodies’ momenta are equal and opposite.
Therefore, the total momentum before interaction equals the total momentum after interaction: m1u1 + m2u2 = m1v1 + m2v2.

items.followUp: A hydraulic press has piston areas of 0.02 m² and 0.50 m². If a force of 100 N is applied to the small piston, find the force on the large piston.

rubric.why: Assesses what is acted on in Pascal’s law.
rubric.description: Identifies that the law concerns pressure applied to an enclosed fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying pressure applied to an enclosed fluid.

rubric.why: Assesses how the applied pressure is transmitted.
rubric.description: States that the pressure is transmitted equally and undiminished through the fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the pressure is transmitted equally or undiminished throughout the fluid.

rubric.why: Assesses the equality of pressure at the two pistons.
rubric.description: Applies Pascal’s law to state that the pressures at the two pistons are equal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for equating the pressures at the pistons.

rubric.description: Uses pressure as force divided by area to derive the force-area relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct equivalent hydraulic-press equation.

modelAnswer: Pascal’s law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally and undiminished in every direction throughout the fluid and to the walls of its container.
In a hydraulic press, let F1 and A1 be the force and area of the small piston, and F2 and A2 those of the large piston.
By Pascal’s law, the pressures at the pistons are equal: P1 = P2.
Since pressure P = F/A, F1/A1 = F2/A2.

items.followUp: Define derived quantities and give two examples.

rubric.why: Assesses the definition of base quantities.
rubric.description: Defines base quantities as independent quantities not defined in terms of other physical quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that base quantities are independent or are not defined in terms of other quantities.

rubric.description: Gives two valid examples of base quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid examples, such as length, mass or time.

modelAnswer: Base quantities are independent physical quantities that are not defined in terms of other physical quantities.

items.followUp: According to Galileo, what happens to the acceleration of a heavy and a light object falling freely in the absence of air resistance?

rubric.why: Assesses Galileo’s claim about freely falling bodies.
rubric.description: States that freely falling bodies have the same acceleration or fall at the same rate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that freely falling bodies have the same acceleration or fall at the same rate.

rubric.why: Assesses the independence from mass and the condition for the claim.
rubric.description: States that the acceleration does not depend on the bodies’ masses when air resistance is absent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that acceleration is independent of mass, with air resistance absent or neglected.

modelAnswer: Galileo’s view was that, in the absence of air resistance, all bodies falling freely have the same acceleration.
Their acceleration does not depend on their masses.

items.followUp: A 0.5 kg object moves in a circle of radius 2 m at 4 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force.

rubric.why: Assesses the definition of centripetal force.
rubric.description: Defines centripetal force as directed towards the centre of a circular path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the direction of the force as towards the centre of circular motion.

rubric.why: Assesses the formula for centripetal force.
rubric.description: Gives the formula for centripetal force.

modelAnswer: Centripetal force is the force directed towards the centre of a circular path that keeps an object moving in that path.
